# Project Overview
**nUIget** is a VS Code extension providing a Visual Studio-style NuGet package manager UI. Users can search, install, update, and remove NuGet packages across multiple .NET projects and sources. Built with TypeScript 6, React 19 (webview UI), esbuild (3 bundles), and the VS Code Extension API. Communicates with the dotnet CLI and NuGet HTTP APIs (v3 service index, registration, search).

## Project Structure
| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `src/extension.ts` | Extension entry point — registers commands, panels, sidebar |
| `src/services/` | Backend: NuGet API client, CLI wrapper, config parser, caching, logging |
| `src/webview/NuGetPanel.ts` | Main panel message router (40+ cases), cross-panel sync |
| `src/webview/NuGetSidebarPanel.ts` | Sidebar provider, background update checks |
| `src/webview/app/` | React app: App.tsx (state machine), tabs, components, hooks |
| `src/webview/sidebar/` | React sidebar: SidebarApp.tsx, PackageRow, SectionHeader |
| `src/test/` | Test helpers, mocks (`vscode.ts`), fixtures (`.csproj`, `project.assets.json`) |
| `resources/` | Extension icons (SVG, PNG) |
| `.github/` | CI workflow, Copilot instructions, agents, prompts |
| `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code pointers to the `.github/` agent resources |

# Agent Guidelines
- **Use Context7 for Documentation:** Discover the current host's tools, then use `resolve-library-id` and `query-docs` for version-specific library documentation.
- **Use Context7 for VS Code, .NET, and NuGet docs too:** Query `/websites/code_visualstudio_api` for the VS Code extension API, `/dotnet/docs` for the dotnet CLI, and `/websites/learn_microsoft_en-us_nuget` for NuGet; resolve the ID again if one is missing. No Microsoft Learn MCP server is configured, and its search does not index the VS Code extension API. Fetch a known documentation URL directly when a full page is needed.
- **2.0 plan in progress:** `docs/plans/2026-10-11-nuiget-2.0-execution-plan.md` is the execution plan for the 2.0 re-architecture, run on the `labs/2.0` branch under `docs/plans/RUN.md` with one tracker row per item in `docs/plans/STATUS.md`. Work one item at a time, cite item, finding and ADR IDs in commits, and read the plan's §1–§4 before starting. `ARCHITECTURE.md` describes 1.x until its 2.0 section lands; verify its claims against code before relying on them (known drift is in the plan's Appendix A).

## Agent Resource Maintenance

- Scope React and accessibility instructions to webview code; do not apply SSR,
  Server Actions, or browser-app data fetching patterns to this extension.
- Treat upstream resources as templates, not authority over this repository's
  architecture. Preserve local adaptations when updating from Awesome Copilot.
- Use `git-commit` as the single commit skill. A version bump or publish request
  does not authorize a commit, push, tag, or memory write.
- Use the GitHub Actions efficiency/hardening skills for CI-specific work and
  the Technical Writer agent for existing documentation. Do not install tools
  or change repository/account settings merely because a resource suggests it.
- Claude Code reads the same resources through `CLAUDE.md` (imports this file),
  `.claude/rules/` (path-scoped pointers to `.github/instructions/`),
  `.claude/skills/` (symlinks to `.github/skills/`) and `.claude/agents/`
  (pointers to `.github/agents/`). When adding, renaming, or rescoping an
  instruction, skill, prompt, or agent, update the matching `.claude/` entry.
  `.claude/settings.json` pre-approves the build, test and bench commands and
  denies publishing and force-push; extend its allowlist when adding a new
  verification script.
- The obsolete offline-support implementation prompt has been retired. Base new
  offline work on `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the current package-service implementation.

## MANDATORY: Read ARCHITECTURE.md Before Making Changes
**ARCHITECTURE.md is the single source of truth** for all technical details: component hierarchy, message protocol, state management patterns, caching strategies, auth flow, security, performance patterns, and sidebar architecture. This file (copilot-instructions.md) only contains agent rules, build commands, and gotchas/pitfalls — it does NOT duplicate architecture details.

**Before** modifying any TypeScript, React, or CSS file, read the relevant section(s) of ARCHITECTURE.md to understand:
- How components communicate (message types, forwardRef routing, cross-panel sync)
- State ownership (what lives in App.tsx vs tab components vs sidebar)
- Caching layers (backend LRUMap, frontend useRef<LRUMap>, WorkspaceCache)
- Performance patterns (batchedPromiseAll, failedEndpointCache, HTTP/2 session pool)
- Security constraints (input validation, credential redaction, CSP)

Failing to consult ARCHITECTURE.md risks re-introducing bugs, duplicating logic, or breaking established patterns.

## MANDATORY: Tests
Tests are **NOT OPTIONAL**. Every code change must satisfy all of the following:

1. **Run ALL test suites before finishing.** Run these commands and confirm **all pass** before declaring work complete:
   - `npm test` — Unit and integration tests using the configured Vitest projects
   - `npm run bench` — Backend benchmarks
   - `npm run test:ui` — UI tests (ExTester/Selenium, requires VS Code + VSIX build). If this command fails due to environment constraints (no display, CI-only), note it in your summary but do not block on it.
   If any test or benchmark fails, fix it before moving on. Never submit, commit, or declare work complete with failures.
2. **Update existing tests.** When changing behavior, update every test that covers the changed code path so it reflects the new behavior. Do NOT delete or skip tests to make the suite pass.
3. **Add new tests.** When adding new functions, message handlers, React components, hooks, or non-trivial logic, write tests for them. Follow the existing patterns in the codebase (see `src/test/` helpers and fixtures). At minimum, cover the happy path and one error/edge case.
4. **Maintain benchmark suite.** When adding or changing performance-sensitive code (services, caching, HTTP, parsing), add or update benchmarks in `src/test/benchmarks/`. Service benchmarks use `mockServiceHttp(service)` from `setup.ts` — never use MSW (it can't intercept HTTP/2). After performance-affecting changes, regenerate the baseline: `npm run bench:save` and commit `benchmarks/baseline.json`.
5. **Maintain coverage thresholds.** The CI pipeline enforces minimum coverage (65% lines, 50% branches, 55% functions). New code must not drop coverage below these thresholds. Run `npm run test:coverage` to verify.
6. **Never skip, `.only`, or comment-out tests** as a workaround. If a test is flaky or blocking, fix the root cause.

Test infrastructure details are in the **Testing** section of ARCHITECTURE.md.

## MANDATORY: VSIX Packaging Verification
After making changes to TypeScript files (especially `NuGetService.ts`, `NuGetPanel.ts`, or `extension.ts`), run `npm run package:vsix` to verify the build succeeds. This runs the full pipeline: `npm ci → check-types → test → lint+bundle → vsce package`. TypeScript errors (typos, missing properties) will break VSIX packaging even if `npm run watch` succeeds.

## MANDATORY: Documentation Updates
After completing ANY feature, fix, or change, update these files:

| File | Update When |
|------|-------------|
| **CHANGELOG.md** | New features → `### Added`, bug fixes → `### Fixed`, behavior changes → `### Changed` |
| **ARCHITECTURE.md** | New message types, state patterns, services, data flows, capabilities |
| **README.md** | User-facing feature changes, new settings/commands |
| **copilot-instructions.md** | New gotchas or common issues |

### CHANGELOG.md Rules
- Always add entries under an `## [Unreleased]` section at the top of the changelog (below the header). If the section already exists, append to it.
- For `### Added` entries: write the **bold headline** followed by a brief description (e.g., `- **New Feature** — Short explanation of what it does`).
- For `### Fixed` and `### Changed` entries: only write the **bold headline** per bullet (e.g., `- **Some Fix**`). Do NOT add descriptions, explanations, or details after the headline.
- Never edit or modify content under previously released version sections — only the `## [Unreleased]` section may be changed.

### ARCHITECTURE.md vs copilot-instructions.md — What Goes Where
These two files serve different purposes. **Never duplicate content between them.**

| | **ARCHITECTURE.md** | **copilot-instructions.md** |
|---|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Describes *how the system works* (descriptive) | Tells agents *how to work on it* (prescriptive) |
| **Audience** | Any developer needing to understand the codebase | AI agents making changes |
| **Content** | Component architecture, message protocol tables, state management patterns, caching strategies, auth flow, security model, performance patterns, data flows, code examples | Agent rules, mandatory checks, build/test commands, gotchas & pitfalls (issue→solution tables) |
| **Add here when** | New component, message type, state pattern, service, cache layer, API integration, data flow, or architectural decision | New bug trap, footgun, or "don't do X" rule discovered during development |
| **Style** | Explanatory sections with diagrams/code blocks | Terse tables and bullet points |
| **Example** | "The sidebar uses `parseSearchQuery()` returning `{ mode, filterText }` to drive all rendering..." | "Browse section removed — No Browse `SectionHeader` exists. Don't re-add." |

**Rule of thumb:** If it explains *what* or *how* the system works → ARCHITECTURE.md. If it warns about a mistake or prescribes a workflow → copilot-instructions.md.

## Build and Run
```bash
npm install          # Install dependencies
npm run watch        # Build (watch mode) — F5 to launch Extension Host
npm run watch:v2     # Same for the 2.0 entry points (launch configuration "Run 2.0"); not together with watch
npm run package:vsix # Runs: npm ci → check-types → test → lint+bundle → vsce package
npm run check:vsix   # After a build: fails if the VSIX would contain an unexpected file or lack a required one
```

### Testing
```bash
npm test               # Run all unit tests (backend + frontend) — MANDATORY before finishing
npm run bench          # Run all benchmarks — MANDATORY before finishing
npm run test:ui        # UI tests (ExTester/Selenium) — MANDATORY (env-dependent, see Rule 1)
npm run test:watch      # Watch mode (unit tests)
npm run test:backend    # Backend tests only (Node.js)
npm run test:frontend   # Frontend tests only (jsdom)
npm run test:coverage   # Generate coverage report
npm run bench:save      # Save benchmark baseline (commit after perf changes)
npm run bench:compare   # Compare current run against baseline
```
The VS Code task "Run Tests" (`Ctrl+Shift+T` or Task menu) runs `npm test` with output visible in terminal.

**Test:** Open a folder with .csproj files in Extension Host (not nuiget folder). Command Palette → "nUIget: Manage NuGet Packages" or right-click .csproj.

# Gotchas & Pitfalls

Two sets while 1.x and 2.0 coexist on `labs/2.0`. Rows under **2.0 gotchas** apply to `src/core/**`,
`src/protocol/**`, `src/host/**`, `src/webview/{main,sidebar-next,shared}/**` and `src/extension.next.ts`.
Rows under **1.x gotchas** apply to the legacy code (`src/services/**`, `src/webview/{app,sidebar}/**`,
`src/webview/NuGet*.ts`, `src/extension.ts`) and to the shared tooling until the flip; do not carry 1.x state
patterns into 2.0 code.

## 2.0 gotchas

Seeded from the execution plan (decisions D1–D13, Appendix B). Item IDs name where each defect is fixed.

| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| "Tests pass" is not "compiles" | Vitest transpiles without type-checking. `npx tsc --noEmit` → 0 is a separate gate for every item; never infer it from a green test run. That command reads the root `tsconfig.json` only, which leaves the test files out: also run `npm run check-types` (adds `tsconfig.test.json` and `tsconfig.vitest.json`), which CI's Build & Package and UI jobs run first (N69). |
| Missing neighbour module | Never stub a module that a later item creates so `tsc` passes. Mark the item `blocked` in `docs/plans/STATUS.md` and stop. |
| Frozen contracts | `src/protocol/**`, `src/core/contracts.ts` and `docs/adr/**` change only in the items that name them, behind the `.claude/.contract-change` sentinel (D6). Never widen a contract to fix a type error. |
| Import boundaries | Follow `.github/instructions/core-boundaries.instructions.md`. Core never imports host, extension, webview, services, React or `vscode` values; `sidebar-next` is not exempt (P0.7). |
| Extension host is Node 18.15 | VS Code 1.85 baseline (D10). No Node ≥ 20 API in 2.0 code; core uses `PromiseLike`, and `Thenable` appears only in `contracts.ts`. |
| .NET SDK floor is 10 | Noun-first `dotnet package add/remove/list --project` only; no verb-first builders or SDK capability table. A project that resolves SDK < 10 is `unsupported` and read-only (D13). |
| CPM and `--no-restore` | Never pass `--no-restore` to `package add` on a CPM project, and refuse CPM `add`/`update` until the mutator lands (D7, P1.10, P6.3). SDK 8 writes `<Version>` into the project (N1); SDK 10.0.401 does not, and the rule stays. Evidence: `docs/adr/004-sdk-probes.md`. |
| SDK 10 reformats `Directory.Packages.props` | Every `dotnet package add --version` rewrites the file (blank lines and final newline stripped), even when the version is unchanged. Treat the props file as modified after any add (P6.3). |
| Quarry is read-only and its notes are stale | Copy from the quarry working tree, never from `git show f837f34:`; never rebase or merge it; verify every quarry `STATUS.md` claim against the tree (D3). |
| Evidence must be tracked | No decision may cite a gitignored capture such as `__fixtures__/.scratch`. Promote probe output to tracked, redacted fixtures (plan §2.6). |
| Transient failure cached as a result | Cache successes and definitive failures only. Never cache spawn errors, timeouts or cancellations of an SDK probe (P1.6), and never turn a feed outage into a 24 h miss (P4.4). |
| Empty is not unknown | An unreachable source yields `sourcesUnavailable`, not an empty update, search or vulnerability result (P4.6, P4.7, P4.8). A vulnerability list from a source read in part is unknown: leave `vulnerabilities` absent, never `[]`. |
| Project paths compared verbatim | Normalize with `normalizeProjectPath` before matching project paths; Windows casing and separators differ (P1.7). |
| CLI output reaches logs unredacted | Redact dotnet output and argv before logging or passing them to `onCommand` (P1.5, P1.10). |
| Unbounded persisted cache entries | Persisted cache entries have an 8 MB byte budget (P1.4); icon data URIs go through it, not around it (P4.4). |
| Restore output in project fixtures | `**/obj/` is ignored, with an exception for `src/core/project/__fixtures__/**/obj/`: a fixture's `obj/project.assets.json` is tracked and read in place. A test that needs a writable project directory uses `createScratchDir` from `__fixtures__/scratch.ts` and cleans up in `afterEach`; never read a file that is only in `__fixtures__/.scratch` (plan §2.6, P2.2). |
| `git status` misses a new file | Plain `git status --short` can leave out a new file in a directory that already has tracked files (git's untracked cache; seen with `docs/adr/009-catalog.md` and `src/core/credentials/`). Before a commit check with `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`, and add files by explicit path. |
| Local shell differs from the CI runners | The runners set `DOTNET_ROOT` and `NUIGET_SDK_TESTS=1`; a local shell may have neither, and then the real-SDK tests are skipped and the runner resolves a different executable. Before pushing a change to `src/core/cli` or to code that runs `dotnet`, also run `DOTNET_ROOT="$(dirname "$(command -v dotnet)")" NUIGET_SDK_TESTS=1 npx vitest run --project backend src/core/cli`. A test that asserts on the executable passes `resolveExecutable` to `DefaultDotnetRunner` (finding N48). |
| `child_process` outside the CLI module | `grep -rln child_process src/core --include='*.ts'` lists only `src/core/cli/*` (without `--include` it also lists handoff notes that mention the word); `src/core/cli/commands.test.ts` asserts it. Processes are spawned with argv, never through a shell (ADR-003, P1.6). |
| Second import-restriction block | ESLint's flat configuration replaces rule options, it does not merge them. Never add another `@typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports` block for files a fence already covers; extend `LAYERS` or `LEGACY_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST` in `eslint.config.mjs`. |
| Sibling imports dodge folder patterns | From `src/webview/sidebar-next`, 1.x code is `../app/x`, which `**/webview/app/**` does not match. The webview fence therefore also denies `**/app/**`, `**/sidebar/**` and `../NuGet*`; do not name a 2.0 webview folder `app` or `sidebar`. |
| A red CI run is not always a code failure | Read `gh run view <id> --log-failed` first. Three known environmental failures: `E2E (1.85.0)` or `UI` stops with "Failed to download and unzip VS Code" or a ChromeDriver download error before any test ran (finding N37); or either `E2E` job (seen on `1.85.0` and on `stable`) reports `Update Flow › install old version then update to latest` failing its first assertion (".csproj should contain 3.13.3") about 10 s into the suite, with VS Code downloaded and every other test passing (finding N44: the legacy test sleeps a fixed 10 s for the suite's first `dotnet` command); or an `E2E` job (seen on the 1.x `stable` job) exits with code 1 before Mocha ran a test, VS Code downloaded and "CodeWindow: detected unresponsive" in its log, while the other `E2E` jobs of the run pass (finding N65). For any of them, re-run with `gh run rerun <id> --failed`, change no code or test in the item whose run went red, and never mark a job `continue-on-error` to hide it. A second identical failure on the same SHA is a stop-and-ask. Since the third sighting of N44 the `e2e` job runs `dotnet --version && dotnet msbuild -version` before the tests; if the same assertion still fails with that step in place, that is a stop-and-ask as well. |
| Two watchers, one `dist/` | `npm run watch` (1.x) and `npm run watch:v2` (2.0) both write `dist/{extension,webview,sidebar}.js`. Never run them together, and never add a script named `watch:<x>` expecting `npm run watch` to pick it up: `watch` lists its scripts explicitly. The "Run 2.0" launch configuration runs whatever was last built into `dist/`. |
| Analysis files in the VSIX | `--analyze` writes metafiles to `out/esbuild/`, never to `dist/`: `.vscodeignore` does not exclude JSON under `dist/`. |
| `.vscodeignore` regressions | The VSIX contains only `dist/*.js`, `dist/*.css`, `resources/`, `package.json`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `LICENSE`. After a build, `npm run check:vsix` fails for any other file and for a missing bundle or manifest icon. A new top-level file needs a `.vscodeignore` entry; a file that must ship needs an `ALLOWED_PATTERNS` entry in `scripts/check-vsix-contents.mjs`. |
| `docs/protocol.md` edited by hand | The file is generated from `src/protocol/messages.ts`. After a change to `RequestMap` or `EventMap` (contract items only), run `npm run docs:protocol` and commit the result; `npm run docs:protocol:check` fails in the Lint job of CI when the file has drifted. A new request or event type also needs its key in the records of `src/protocol/guards.ts`; `tsc` fails until it is there. |
| Stale files in `dist/` | Builds do not clean `dist/`. After switching between `node esbuild.mjs` and `node esbuild.mjs --v2`, files of the other entry set (for example the 1.x CSS) remain and would be packaged. Delete `dist/` before packaging a different entry set. |
| Mock panel disposes without end | `createMockWebviewPanel()` of `src/test/__mocks__/vscode.ts` fires `onDidDispose` on every `dispose()` and its events ignore the `disposables` argument, so `MainPanelHost.dispose()` (which disposes its panel) recurses until the stack overflows. VS Code reports a disposal once. A test that opens the 2.0 main panel hands `createWebviewPanel` a panel whose `dispose` fires once (`createFakePanel` in `src/extension.next.test.ts` and the harness's panel in `src/test/harness/harness.ts`; finding N58). |
| Bench under `src/core` is silently not run | `vitest.config.mts` discovers benchmarks under `src/test/benchmarks/**` only; a `*.bench.ts` next to its module is neither run nor type-checked and nothing reports that. Until P8.2 moves the benches (D8, N40), a 2.0 bench is `src/test/benchmarks/core-<module>.bench.ts`. |
| Bundle ceilings are a local gate | `node esbuild.mjs --production --analyze` (with `--v2` for the 2.0 entries, which have their own table) is the only place the ceilings are checked; CI builds without `--analyze` until P7.2. Run it after any 2.0 webview item and paste the sizes in the STATUS note (N63). Run it after any item that touches `src/core/**`, `src/host/**` or `src/extension.next.ts` as well (the 2.0 extension was at 93.6 % after P4); an item whose build would cross a ceiling is a stop-and-ask with the measured delta and the top inputs of the metafile, never a silent raise. |
| Test asserts the order of two asynchronous effects | Two watcher flushes that each read a directory (lock file, assets file) finish in either order; a test that fires both and expects their invalidations in a fixed order fails now and then (finding N60: 7 of 40 runs). Fire and await one effect before the next, or compare as a set. After writing a test with timers and real file I/O, run it a few dozen times: `for i in $(seq 1 40); do npx vitest run <file> \|\| break; done`. |
| Jest-typed matcher packages under Vitest | `@types/jest-axe` (and anything depending on `@types/jest`) augments the `jest` namespace, which `tsconfig.vitest.json` never loads, and puts a second set of `describe`/`it`/`expect` globals next to `vitest/globals`. `jest-axe` is typed by `src/test/jest-axe.d.ts` (a script file: no top-level import or export, or the `declare module` stops being a declaration), and the matcher is declared on Vitest's `Matchers<R, T>` interface in `src/test/setup-frontend.ts` with Vitest's own type parameters. Never add `@types/jest`. |
| Colour literal in a 2.0 webview file | `src/test/lint/webview-colours.test.ts` fails for a hex colour or a colour function (`rgb(`, `hsl(`, …) in any file under `src/webview/{shared,main,sidebar-next}` except `tokens.css`, tests included. Use a `--nuiget-color-*` token; add a token to `tokens.css` (an alias of a `--vscode-*` variable) when none fits, and its name to `webview-tokens.test.ts` if a primitive relies on it. |
| Buttons inside `role="option"` | axe `nested-interactive` fails for a button inside an option, also at `tabIndex={-1}`, and a screen reader cannot reach it. Row actions live in the `aria-hidden` sibling container of `Row` (`actions` prop, `IconButton` with `tabIndex={-1}`), and every one of them has a key in `Listbox` (Enter, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, Delete, Shift+F10). Never add a pointer-only action. |
| Attributes on the row wrapper | The `role="presentation"` wrapper of `Row` carries `className`, `data-*` and the measuring ref, nothing else. An `aria-*` attribute or a `tabIndex` there makes it a child of the listbox that is no option (axe `aria-required-children`). `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` go on the option. |
| Inline style in 2.0 webviews | Only `cssVars()` with `--nuiget-*` custom properties goes into a `style` prop; the stylesheet owns the real property (`height`, `transform`, `width`). Never `style={{ … }}` with a layout or colour property, and never `document.body.style` (ADR-006). The primitive tests read the `style` attribute and fail for anything else. |
| `useVirtualizer` mocked in tests | Never mock `@tanstack/react-virtual` in a 2.0 test. Call `installFakeLayout()` from `src/webview/shared/primitives/testSupport.ts` in `beforeEach` and its return value in `afterEach`, and let the real virtualizer run. Stubbing `getBoundingClientRect` alone is not enough: the virtualizer reads `offsetHeight`, and a `Listbox` then renders no row at all. |
| axe rule skipped in jsdom | "No violations" is also true of a rule axe could not run: without `document.elementFromPoint` (jsdom has none) `aria-hidden-focus` ends as incomplete. `installFakeLayout()` provides it; a test of markup that exists for one rule asserts `axeRuleOutcome(results, '<rule>')` is `'passes'`. |
| New primitive without its stylesheet import | Every module in `src/webview/shared/primitives` imports `./primitives.css`, and so does `index.ts`; a primitive imported on its own would otherwise render unstyled. New rules go into that one file, with the class prefix `nuiget-` and tokens only (`src/test/lint/webview-stylesheets.test.ts`). `testSupport.ts` is never exported from `index.ts`. |
| Webview state compared with the event's `generation` | The `generation` of a `resources/invalidated` event is a sequence number. An ok response is compared with `keys[].generation` of the same key only (`bus.listedGeneration(key)`); equal, absent or no generation at all means current. Never write that comparison in a feature: use `useResource` in `src/webview/shared/store`. |
| Requests that follow a pending selection | Data requests follow `useSession().committed`, never `session` (committed plus this surface's unanswered intents): the host may answer an intent with another project. Render toggles and selectors from `session`. |
| Clearing pending on any snapshot | A pending intent leaves when its own `session/set` is answered, not when some snapshot arrives; otherwise selecting B and then A flashes B. Do not add a "clear pending" action to the session reducer. |
| Re-requesting `projects/list` on invalidation | The projects slice does not ask again when `projects` is invalidated; the host follows with `projects/changed`. The harness's client model and the e2e expectations rely on that request count. |
| Resource keys built in the webview | Build a key from the path exactly as the host sent it (`resourceKeys.installed(snapshot.selectedProject)`); the host lists keys verbatim in `resources/invalidated`. A webview cannot import `normalizeProjectPath` (core), and must not lower-case or re-join a path. |
| Host messages in a component test | Use `createFakeHost()` from `src/webview/shared/bus/testSupport.ts` and wrap what the host says in `act` (`await act(async () => { host.respond(…); await Promise.resolve(); })`). Do not dispatch `MessageEvent`s on `window` by hand (the bus's own test of its `window` default in `MessageBus.test.ts` is the one place) and do not mock the bus. |
| 2.0 webview file named `Sidebar.tsx` or `App.tsx` | The import fence matches a path segment `sidebar` or `app` without regard to case, so `import './Sidebar'` fails lint as 1.x code. Name the file after what it is (`SidebarView.tsx`); do not add it to `LEGACY_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST`. |
| `acquireVsCodeApi` at module top level | It may be called once per page. A 2.0 entry declares it locally and calls it inside `if (rootElement)`, creates the bus there and hands it down through `StoreProvider`; a second caller, or a call in a module that tests import, breaks the entry. |
| Removing a row when an operation succeeds | The sidebar removes nothing by guessing: a row leaves when the host's new list no longer has it (`resources/invalidated` → `installed/get`). A row is busy from the call to `run()` (the ops slice) and from `ops/progress`; do not delete from the list in an outcome handler, and do not blank the list while it revalidates. |
| An operation that waits in the queue has no `ops/progress` | The queue reports progress for a *running* workflow only; the surface that asked gets a `queued` stream chunk on its request, without projects or packages. `useOpsActions().run()` records the operation from the call, with the projects and packages of its payload, and keeps it until the request settles (N61, P5.4), so a feature uses `isPackageBusy` alone. Never keep a pending set of your own in a feature, and never start an operation with `bus.request('ops/…')` directly: that row would not be busy while it waits. |
| A 2.0 entry without its stylesheet import | Both 2.0 entries import `../shared/tokens.css` and their own stylesheet (`main.css`, `sidebar.css`); that import is what makes a `--v2` build write `dist/webview.css` and `dist/sidebar.css`. `npm run check:vsix` requires both, and the `ui-v2` job runs it on the build ExTester packaged (N62, closed at P5.3). Locally: `rm -rf dist && NUIGET_V2=1 npm run package && npm run check:vsix`. |
| A 2.0 VSIX and the `v2` suites need `NUIGET_V2=1` | `vsce` and ExTester always run `vscode:prepublish`, which builds the 1.x entries over whatever `--v2` wrote; a 2.0 VSIX comes only from `NUIGET_V2=1` (`esbuild.mjs` reads it as `--v2`). The same variable selects the `v2-*` e2e files in `.vscode-test.mjs`: `NUIGET_V2=1 npm run test:e2e` after a `--v2` build, `NUIGET_V2=1 npm run test:ui:v2 -- --storage /tmp/nuiget-ui-v2` for the UI suite. Unset it before running the 1.x suites, and `rm -rf dist` when switching entry sets. A v2 test waits with a bounded poll, never a fixed sleep, restores `e2e-workspace/TestProject.csproj`, imports nothing from `src/test/ui/helpers`, and finds a webview by its root test id (`nuiget-app`, `nuiget-sidebar`): with the panel and the sidebar open there are two `iframe.webview`, in no fixed order. |
| Call at module level in a 2.0 webview module | The barrel `primitives/index.ts` puts every primitive into every bundle that imports it, and esbuild keeps any module-level call it cannot prove pure (`React.memo(…)`, `[…].join()`), used or not (N63). Write constants as literals, mark a component factory `/* @__PURE__ */` (`src/test/lint/webview-icons-pure.test.ts` holds this for the icons), and paste the `--v2 --production --analyze` sidebar bytes after the item, not after the first edit. |
| Two selections in one listbox | In a multi-selectable `Listbox` (`selectedIds`) `aria-selected` is the bulk set and `aria-current` the row whose details show. Never render a checkbox or any focusable element inside the option (`nested-interactive`): the check mark is an `aria-hidden` span, and Space, Ctrl/Cmd+click and a click on the mark toggle it. A test that counts rows looks inside the list (`within(list)`): the header's `<select>` elements have options too. |
| `allProjects` is not a `useResource` | The fan-out has no generation and its key is never in `resources/invalidated` (ADR-009). The slice asks again when an invalidation names `projects` or any `installed:` key and applies its latest request only; never compare a generation on its chunks. A chunk (metadata included) arrives only before the answer of its request: the bus drops anything for an answered request. |
| Agent, `fetch` or `rejectUnauthorized` in `Transport` | `Transport` passes no `agent` to `http(s).request`: under `http.proxySupport: on` a defined agent bypasses the VS Code proxy and under `override` it is discarded (ADR-005, `docs/adr/005-proxy-matrix.md`). Never add an `https.Agent`, `rejectUnauthorized: false`, `undici` or the global `fetch`; HTTP/2 only through the allow-list and the injected proxy predicate, with the sticky h2→h1 downgrade. |
| Package id or version in a file path | `isValidPackageId` accepts `.` and `..` (dots are legal in ids). Validate, join, then check the resolved path is still under its folder, as `offlineNuspecPath` in `src/core/feeds/offline.ts` does; never `path.join` a webview-supplied id on the strength of the validator alone. |
| XML from a package | A nuspec is package content: `parseNuspec` refuses any document with a DOCTYPE before parsing, so no entity a package declares is expanded, and validates before the lenient `XMLParser`. Parse other package XML the same way; `htmlEntities: true` still decodes `&amp;` and `&#169;`. |
| `dotnet package search` output | Never `JSON.parse(stdout)`; use `extractCliSearchOutput` in `src/core/feeds/search.ts` (prefix lines are real on this SDK). A bad source is `problems[]` with exit 0, an HTTP source without `allowInsecureConnections` exit 1 with JSON; `sourceName` is the configured name or the `--source` value as given; never `--take` with `--exact-match`. Captures: `src/core/feeds/__fixtures__/cli-search/`. |
| Flat container has no policy | `FlatContainerClient` filters nothing. Filter with `filterAllowedSources` before `nuspec`, `packageSize`, `versionIndex` or `icon`, as `registration.ts`, `icons.ts` and `metadataResolver.ts` do; `src/core/feeds/policy.test.ts` fails when an id reaches a source the mapping does not allow. |
| `batchedPromiseAll` rethrows | One rejected worker fails the whole batch after it completes. Feed code isolates each package with its own try/catch (`updates.ts`, `enricher.ts`), so one package cannot fail a check or an enrichment. |
| `'all'` resource keys are never written | `package/versions` and `package/metadata` query one resource per allowed source; a key built with `sourceUrl: undefined` (`resourceKeys.versions(id, undefined, …)`, `resourceKeys.metadata(id, v, undefined)`) is a defect (N70). |
| Incomplete feed answers are rejections inside the Catalog | A compute that ends with `sourcesUnavailable`, `offline` or no metadata throws `IncompleteResultError(value)`; `queryWithRetry` is the only catch and keeps the generation. Never catch-all around a Catalog query, and never `coordinator.invalidate` from inside a read to uncache it. |
| A recovered source invalidates nothing | The monitor runs no `dotnet`: it probes the sources of chains that reads registered (`FeedContexts.registered()`), restarted by `onDidRegister`; `dotnet nuget config paths` for a project directory runs in `ProjectContextProvider.get`, whose pending walk `computeInstalled` registers with `FeedContexts` before awaiting it, and in `FeedContexts.forDirectory` only for a directory no computation has registered (any directory read, `sources(…, { configFiles: true })` included); the harness holds count walks, so a scenario that asks `sources/list` while a walk is held counts one more. A health pass reports through `sources/health`; webviews re-request what they showed as unavailable; never call `invalidate` from a health pass. A failed source stays in `failed()` until a check settles it; expiry only allows the retry (N71). |
| axe misses a portal | `Dialog` and `Popover` render into `document.body`, outside the container that `render()` returns; `axe(container)` then checks the page without the dialog and passes. A test of a layer runs `axe(document.body)` and asserts `axeRuleOutcome(results, 'aria-dialog-name')` is `'passes'`. Every layer needs a name (`title`, `label` or `labelledBy`). |
| Escape or focus handled outside the layer stack | Only the topmost layer of `primitives/layers.ts` answers Escape, traps focus or closes on an outside press. A feature that opens something over a dialog uses `Dialog`, `ConfirmDialog` or `Popover`, never its own overlay or a `keydown` listener on `document`, or Escape closes two things at once. |
| A rejected promise awaited after the host answers | Vitest reports an unhandled rejection as an error and exits non-zero while every test passes; a `grep` of the `Tests` line hides it. Attach the handler when the promise is created (`const outcome = slice.add(…).then(() => 'ok', error => error.message)`), and read a gate's exit code, not only its counts. |
| Harness: a read that cannot be held | In `src/test/harness` a computation of `installed/get` can be held at `nuget config paths` only (`dotnetCalls.configPaths(dir)`): the SDK probe is cached per directory after its first answer. A resource that the coordinator has cached is answered without any `dotnet` call, so set the hold before the first surface is resolved, or invalidate first (`refresh`). A scenario waits with `settle`/`expectState` and moves the clock with `advance`; `vi.waitFor` advances the fake clock by its interval on every check, so advance explicitly past a watcher debounce before asserting that nothing happened earlier. |

## 1.x gotchas (removed at P8)

These rows describe the legacy architecture and the shared tooling. P8.2 deletes the section together with
the legacy code; before that, P7.5 reviews which tooling rows still hold for 2.0.

### Known Issues
| Issue | Status |
|-------|--------|
| Dependency vulnerability status is time-sensitive | `@vscode/test-cli` and `@vscode/test-electron` are installed for extension-host E2E tests. **Run `npm audit` when assessing current vulnerabilities; do not infer a clean audit from this document.** |
| TypeScript compiler compatibility | Keep TypeScript 6 while `typescript-eslint` declares `<6.1.0`; do not force TypeScript 7 past the parser's peer range. |
| MSW compatibility | Keep the latest MSW 2.x while `@vitest/mocker` declares an MSW 2 peer dependency. Validate `npm ls --all` after packaging, which runs another install and may reintroduce peer conflicts. |
| `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` peer dep | Version 7.1.1 supports ESLint 10; no peer override is needed. |
| Test CLI's Mocha runs inside the extension host | `@vscode/test-cli` loads Mocha with `require()` inside the VS Code extension host, which is Node 18 on the minimum supported VS Code 1.85. It must therefore keep its own Mocha 11; Mocha 12 is ESM-only and cannot load there. Do not add an `overrides` entry that points the test CLI at the direct `mocha` dependency (that one is for ExTester, which runs on the toolchain's Node). The `E2E (1.85.0)` CI job is the guard. `npm audit` reports four findings through Mocha 11's dependencies; they are development-only and never ship in the VSIX. |
| VS Code declarations | Pin `@types/vscode` to `engines.vscode`'s minimum API version; a caret silently permits newer APIs unavailable to supported users. |
| macOS UI-test IPC socket path | ExTester storage under a long session path exceeds the Unix socket limit. Pass a short temporary directory with `npm run test:ui -- --storage /tmp/nuiget-ui`; reuse downloads and clean only task-created paths. |
| Typed backend message routing | `PanelRequestMessage` and `SidebarRequestMessage` in `NuGetTypes.ts` are discriminated unions used by both backend message handlers. Extend these contracts for new requests; do not reintroduce an untyped `WebviewMessage`. ESLint turns off `no-explicit-any` and `no-non-null-assertion` in test files via override in `eslint.config.mjs`. |
| CI and `package:vsix` use `npm ci` | `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` installs exactly what `package-lock.json` records (ADR-000). The earlier `npm install` exception existed for `@emnapi/*` optional dependencies that are no longer in the lockfile. If `npm ci` reports that the lockfile is out of sync, regenerate it with `npm install --package-lock-only` and commit it; never switch CI back to `npm install`. Locally, `npm run package:vsix` therefore reinstalls `node_modules` on every run. |

### VS Code Extension
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Context menu not showing | Use regex: `resourceFilename =~ /\\.(csproj\|fsproj\|vbproj)$/` |
| Watch task hangs preLaunchTask | Compound `watch` task uses `dependsOn` with `npm: watch:esbuild` + `npm: watch:tsc`. esbuild plugin emits `[watch] build started`/`[watch] build finished`. tsc uses `$tsc-watch` matcher. |
| preLaunchTask fails | Use explicit task label ("watch") not "${defaultBuildTask}" |

### React 19 / Webview
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| "process is not defined" | Add esbuild define for `process.env.NODE_ENV` |
| StrictMode double-render | Expected behavior — verifies cleanup functions |
| **setState updater side effects** | **Never** call `postMessage()` or side effects inside `setState(prev => {...})` — StrictMode may run updaters twice. Derive the operation from the current synchronous ref/state snapshot, then update state and perform the side effect separately. Do not assign a flag inside the updater and read it immediately afterward. |
| **Async setState variable assignment** | **CRITICAL:** Never assign `let x` inside `setState(prev => {...})` and read after — React 19 runs updaters async, `x` stays initial. Use `useRef` mirror pattern (see `transitiveLoadingMetadataRef`). |
| Stale closures in `useCallback([])` | App.tsx uses `useCallback(fn, [])` with individual `useRef` mirrors (`selectedProjectRef`, `selectedSourceRef`, `activeTabRef`, etc.) synced via `useEffect`. SidebarApp.tsx uses the `handleMessageRef` pattern: regular function assigned to `ref.current` each render, one `useEffect([])` listener calls `ref.current(e)`. |
| Inline callbacks defeat React.memo | Extract callbacks to `useCallback([])` (e.g., `handleSashReset`, `handleSashDragEnd`, `handleToggleDep`). Inline arrows create new refs every render. |
| Icons not loading | CSP: `img-src https://api.nuget.org https://*.nuget.org data:;`. Use flat container API, not registration iconUrl. |
| README images not loading | CSP includes: `github.com`, `githubusercontent.com`, `shields.io`, `opencollective.com`, `codecov.io`, `badge.fury.io`, `travis-ci.*`, `appveyor.com`, `coveralls.io`, `snyk.io`, `codacy.com`, `sonarcloud.io`, `badgen.net`, `circleci.com`, `azure/visualstudio` |
| Code blocks not highlighted | `marked-highlight` + `highlight.js/lib/core` with individual languages + `ignoreIllegals: true`. All config in `markdownSetup.ts`. |
| XSS in README | `renderMarkdownToHtml()` in `markdownSetup.ts` handles `DOMPurify.sanitize()` + `marked.parse()` + `upgradeHttpToHttps()`. Never call these separately in components. |
| Colors not adapting | Use `--vscode-*` CSS variables. Light themes need `body.vscode-light` overrides. |
| BrowseTab removed | No `BrowseTab.tsx` component exists. Search, browse results, quick search, and browse details panel are in App.tsx. Don't re-add a BrowseTab component. |
| InstalledTab filter bar removed | No `.installed-filter-bar` exists. Filtering is driven by `externalFilter`/`externalFilterMode` props from App.tsx unified search bar. Don't re-add internal filter state or filter UI to InstalledTab. |
| Unified search bar state in App.tsx | All search state (`searchQuery`, `searchResults`, `quickSearchSuggestions`, `recentSearches`, `showFilterDropdown`, etc.) lives in App.tsx. `parseSearchQuery()` from `utils/parseSearchQuery.ts` drives mode detection. Tabs receive `externalFilter` and `externalFilterMode` props. |

### State Management
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Settings reset on panel close | Use `context.workspaceState` via messages, not just `vscode.getState/setState` |
| Source dropdown resets | Use `settingsLoadedRef` flag to prevent defaults overwriting loaded settings |
| Details panel shows wrong package | Clear both `selectedPackage` AND `selectedTransitivePackage` — mutually exclusive |
| Stale packages on project switch | `selectedProject` effect must `setInstalledPackages([])` before fetching. Without it, stale data triggers `checkPackageUpdates` for the wrong project. |
| Version dropdown "Loading" on re-click | `useRef<LRUMap>` frontend cache. Check cache before fetching. |
| Cache key uses echoed response values | `packageVersions` and `packageMetadata` responses echo `source` (and `includePrerelease`) from the request. Frontend cache keys use echoed values — never `selectedSourceRef.current` or `includePrereleaseRef.current`, which may have changed during the async roundtrip. |
| Installed tab no re-fetch on switch-back | `hasVisitedInstalledTabRef` marks first visit only. Subsequent visits rely on file watcher + cross-panel sync (`retainContextWhenHidden: true`) to keep `installedPackages` current. Don't re-add re-fetch on tab switch. |
| `refreshScoped` vs `refresh` message | `refreshScoped` sets `skipNextUpdateCheckRef.current = true` + re-fetches only installed packages. Used by sidebar-initiated `_notifyMainPanel(operation)`. `refresh` is the full reload path (file watcher, manual refresh). Don't send `refresh` after sidebar operations — costs ~2s extra for redundant `checkPackageUpdates`. |
| installedPackages cascading renders | Content comparison in setter: compare `id@version` joined keys, return `prev` if unchanged |
| Operation results in all-projects mode | `installResult`/`updateResult`/`removeResult` in App.tsx must handle `selectedProjectRef.current === ALL_PROJECTS_SENTINEL`. In all-projects mode, re-fetch via `checkAllProjectsUpdates` + `checkAllProjectsInstalled` instead of single-project `getInstalledPackages`. The `message.projectPath` will be the real project path, not the sentinel — so the old `=== selectedProjectRef.current` guard was always false. |
| Source removal stale closure | `handleMessage` is `useCallback([])` — `sources` state is stale. Backend sends `removedSourceUrl`, frontend compares via `selectedSourceRef.current`. |
| **Transitive metadata ref mirror** | Use `transitiveLoadingMetadataRef = useRef<Set>()` as synchronous mirror. Read ref in prefetch effect, update both ref and state. Required because React 19 defers setState updaters. |
| Transitive spinner stuck | `doResetTransitiveState(false)` must set `loadingTransitive = false` — prevents stuck spinner when reset races with in-flight request. |
| Transitive stale after bulk remove | `bulkRemoveResult` handler must call `resetTransitiveState(true)` after routing. |
| All-projects transitive section | Aggregated single Transitive Packages section appears below per-framework Top-Level sections. Dedup key is `lowerId@versionNormalized`; aggregation is a `useMemo` over `allProjectsTransitiveRows`. Each origin is keyed `(projectPath, chainHash)` where `chainHash` is the FULL root set (`fullChain ?? requiredByChain`, not the 5-item display slice) — TFMs sharing a root set merge into one origin's `frameworks[]`. The details panel renders one block per project via `groupOriginsByProject()` (don't render raw origins — same project would appear multiple times); an empty root set shows a neutral "No traceable top-level package" note, never "Unknown". Loads lazily when section is first expanded. Collapsing does NOT abort the stream (results are kept for re-expansion). The stream is aborted by project switch (`ALL_PROJECTS` ↔ single) and by `refresh`/`refreshScoped`. Don't re-introduce the old "hide transitive in all-projects" guard. |
| Transitive required-by roots | `NuGetProjectService.resolveRoots()` uses per-package reverse BFS with a LOCAL `visited` set — never re-introduce the old shared-`visited` recursion + id-keyed `chainCache`, which poisoned the cache on cyclic graphs and caused false "Required by: unknown". `requiredByChain` holds bare top-level root ids (not arrow-joined chains). |
| All-projects transitive selection | Selection state for transitive packages in all-projects mode stores only `(lowerId, versionNormalized)`. A `useEffect` re-resolves the live row from `aggregatedAllProjectsTransitive` whenever it changes; if no row matches, selection clears. Don't store the resolved row directly — origin chunks streaming in would render it stale. |
| All-projects transitive restore | Restore banner only renders when section is expanded AND at least one project errored. `onRestoreProjectsBatch` debounces concurrent invocations (idempotent: no-op if already running). After restore, `refreshScoped` re-emits per-project transitive chunks. |
| All-projects icon enrichment is two-phase | `checkAllProjectsUpdates`/`checkAllProjectsInstalled` sends initial data immediately, then fires background `resolveAllProjectsIcons()` which sends `allProjectsIcons` message. Don't block initial response on icon resolution. Sidebar skips icon enrichment (compact layout). `multiInstall` context also skips icons. |
| CLI search results are two-phase | `searchPackages` handler sends `searchResults` with `liteMode: true` immediately, then conditionally fires `enrichSearchResultMetadata()` → `searchResultsMetadata` follow-up for CLI-path results (`iconUrl === undefined && verified === undefined`). Both phases guarded by `_latestSearchQuery`. API-path results skip Phase 2. Don't block initial search response on enrichment. |
| Generalized API search routing | `searchPackages()` collects ALL input source URLs first (from `sources` param or `getSources()`), resolves remote+healthy ones via `resolveSourcesForSearch()`, partitions into API-capable (have `searchQueryService`). CLI fallback URLs = `allInputUrls - apiSourceUrls` (filtered healthy) — includes local sources, failed-discovery sources, and sources without SearchQueryService. Results merged with API priority + `.slice(0, searchResultLimit)` cap. `searchPackagesViaApi` sorts multi-source results by 5-tier relevance (`searchRelevanceTier`: exact match → prefix → substring/contains → token match → rest), then totalDownloads desc. After merging CLI results, a second relevance sort runs before the cap. Handles PascalCase fields (BaGet/ProGet) and source-specific `packageBaseAddress` for icons. |
| Multi-project updates not refreshing | `bulkUpdateAllProjectsResult` handler must re-fetch via `checkAllProjectsUpdates` after forwarding to UpdatesTab. |
| Multi Install data isolation | `multiInstallProjectData` is a **separate state** from `allProjectsInstalled` — not cleared on tab switch. `allProjectsInstalled` is for the Installed tab; `multiInstallProjectData` is for the browse results Multi Install dropdown. Backend echoes `context` field in `allProjectsInstalled` response to route correctly. After `bulkInstallResult`, optimistic update + re-fetch via `context: 'multiInstall'`. Multi Install button only visible when `!isInstalled` (package not installed in current project) — avoids scope confusion with single-project Uninstall. |
| Cross-panel sync echo loop | Use `skipSaveRef`/`skipSourceSaveRef`/`skipProjectSaveRef` refs in App.tsx. Set `true` before setState, save effect checks and resets. |
| Restore-after-operations toggle | Replaces the deleted `nuiget.noRestore` config setting. Stored per-workspace under `nuget.restoreEnabled` (positive form, default `true`). Conversion to `OperationContext.skipRestore = !restoreEnabled` happens in `_opCtx()` on both panels. Both panels snapshot `_opCtx()` at message-handler enqueue time — a toggle mid-bulk-op does NOT change in-flight ops. Sidebar `toggleRestore()` writes workspaceState + setContext (`nuiget.restoreEnabled`) + posts `restoreChanged` + calls `NuGetPanel.syncRestore`. Static `syncRestore(value)` only setContext + postMessage (no workspaceState write — avoids double-write race). Migration from legacy `nuiget.noRestore` runs once on activation BEFORE sidebar provider creation, gated by `nuget.restoreEnabledMigrated` flag. Icon convention: filled `$(verified-filled)` = ON (default); outline `$(verified)` = OFF. `view/title` entries are gated on `nuiget.restoreEnabled` context key. Manual "refresh transitive packages" button (NuGetPanel.ts:319-321) calls `restoreProject()` directly — bypasses `OperationContext` by design. |
| `skipNextUpdateCheckRef` skips update re-check | After an operation with known outcome, set `skipNextUpdateCheckRef.current = true` before requesting `getInstalledPackages`. The `[installedPackages]` effect checks and resets the flag, skipping the redundant `checkPackageUpdates`. The `selectedProject` effect resets the flag to `false` — without this, a lingering flag would skip the else-if branch that clears stale updates after project switch. |
| `notifySidebarOfChange` vs `refreshSidebar` | `notifySidebarOfChange(operation)` is the lightweight post-operation path — skips `clearNuGetHttpCache()` and source re-fetch, sends `packageChanged` message for surgical UI updates (including optimistic installed-data removal). Passes `scope` to `checkUpdatesInBackground(true, skipMainPanelNotify=true, scope)` for selective cache invalidation (only affected packages) and scoped project re-checking (only affected project). Cancels the file watcher debounce as its first action so the watcher's `~5s` debounced fire can't double up with the optimistic refresh. `refreshSidebar()` is for manual refresh button only. Don't swap them. |
| `forceRefresh` vs `revalidate` sidebar messages | `forceRefresh` is destructive: clears `installedPackages`/`packageUpdates`/`allProjectsInstalled`/`allProjectsUpdates` immediately (causes empty-state flash), then re-fetches. Used by manual refresh button. `revalidate` is non-destructive: re-fetches in background and only flips loading skeletons when current state is empty. Used by file watcher (`.csproj` change). When adding a new "soft refresh" trigger, prefer `revalidate`. |
| Sidebar single-project op result is optimistic | After a successful single-project `installResult`/`updateResult`/`removeResult`, `SidebarApp.tsx` mutates `installedPackages` directly using `message.packageId`/`message.version`/`message.projectPath` (always present per `NuGetOperations.ts`). Don't re-add the `getInstalledPackages` re-fetch — it caused a visible double-reload. The all-projects branch keeps its own optimistic mutation of `allProjectsInstalled` + `installedPackages`. Re-fetch is only triggered when `message.projectPath !== selectedProjectRef.current` is implicitly handled by the project-switch effect. |
| `checkUpdatesInBackground` scope parameter | Third parameter `scope?: { packageIds?: string[]; projectPath?: string }`. When `packageIds` provided, calls `clearVersionsCacheForPackages(ids)` instead of `clearVersionsCache()`. When `projectPath` provided, only re-checks that project and merges with cached `_pendingProjectUpdates`. Scope is merged when queued via `_forceCheckPending` (union of packageIds, projectPath cleared if different). |
| `checkUpdatesInBackground` skipMainPanelNotify | When the main panel initiates an operation, `notifySidebarOfChange` passes `skipMainPanelNotify=true` to avoid a redundant `refresh` → `getInstalledPackages` → `checkPackageUpdates` → icon resolution cycle on the main panel. Without this, every install/update/remove causes a slow second reload visible to the user. Only callers where the main panel doesn't already know about the change (file watcher, periodic check) should allow full `_notifyMainPanel()`. Sidebar operations use `_notifyMainPanel(operation)` which dispatches `nuiget.refreshPackagesScoped` for a lightweight scoped refresh. |
| Bulk ops must include packageIds | `notifyOtherPanel` calls in `NuGetOperations.ts` bulk functions must include `packageIds` (successful package IDs). `notifySidebarOfChange` merges `packageId` (single) and `packageIds` (bulk) into a single list for selective cache invalidation. Without `packageIds`, bulk operations fall back to full cache clear. |
| Sidebar `packageChanged` updates installed data | The sidebar `packageChanged` handler optimistically updates `allProjectsInstalled` and `installedPackages` for remove operations (mirroring `removeResult`). For install operations, it triggers `checkAllProjectsInstalled` re-fetch since version info is unavailable. `checkUpdatesInBackground` only sends `allProjectsUpdates` and `installedCountUpdate` — it does NOT send the installed packages list. |
| `onPackageChanged` only on success | Single-op handlers (`installPackage`, `updatePackage`, `removePackage`) must only call `NuGetPanel.onPackageChanged?.()` when the operation succeeded. The `success` variable is hoisted outside `withProgress` (e.g. `let installSuccess = false;`). Without this guard, a failed operation still triggers sidebar optimistic updates that remove the package from the updates list. `bulkInstall` must check `results.some(r => r.success)`. |
| Sidebar result `message.success` check | Sidebar's `installResult`/`updateResult`/`removeResult` handler must check `message.success` before optimistically filtering packages from update lists. Without this, a failed sidebar operation incorrectly removes the package from the sidebar's updates. |
| Sidebar `_notifyMainPanel` only on success | `NuGetSidebarProvider._notifyMainPanel()` must only be called after successful operations. For single ops, guard with `if (success)`. For `bulkUpdatePackages`, guard with `failedPackageIds.length < packages.length`. For `bulkUpdateAllProjects`, guard with `totalFailed < totalPackages`. Without this, a failed sidebar operation triggers an unnecessary full main panel refresh. |
| Bulk result `failedPackageIds` scoping | `failedPackageIds` / `perProjectFailedIds` must be declared OUTSIDE the `withProgress` callback — the `_postMessage` call referencing them is after the callback closes. Declaring inside causes `ReferenceError` at runtime. |
| Bulk result enriched payloads | All bulk result messages (`bulkUpdateResult`, `bulkRemoveResult`, `bulkUpdateAllProjectsResult`, `bulkRemoveAllProjectsResult`) include per-package failure data. New bulk operations must follow this pattern for optimistic UI updates. |
| `refreshDebounceRef` in App.tsx | The `refresh` handler uses 300ms debounce to collapse rapid refresh messages from sidebar operations. Don't remove — without it, 3 quick sidebar ops trigger 3 full main panel reloads. |
| SourceSettingsOverlay state ownership | Source settings form state (`addSourceUrl`, `addSourceName`, `addingSource`, `confirmRemoveSource`, etc.) lives INSIDE `SourceSettingsOverlay.tsx`, NOT in App.tsx. App.tsx forwards `addSourceResult` via `sourceSettingsRef.current?.handleAddSourceResult()`. Don't re-add these state vars to App.tsx. |

### Sidebar
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Activity Bar badge removed | Badge feature was removed. No `setBadge`, `_clearBadge`, `_buildBadgeTooltip`, `_pendingBadgeCount`, `_pendingBadgeTooltip`, `_showActivityBarBadge`, or `nuiget.showActivityBarBadge` setting exists. Don't re-add. |
| Search mode model | Shared `parseSearchQuery(query)` supports `default`, `browse`, `installed`, `updates`, and `vulnerable` modes. The main panel supports `@vulnerable`; the sidebar deliberately excludes that prefix from its suggestions and supports only `@installed` and `@updates`. Never check `installedExpanded`/`updatesExpanded` outside default mode. |
| Browse section removed | No Browse `SectionHeader` exists. Browse results render directly when `searchMode === 'browse'` (plain text + Enter). |
| Recent searches removed | No state, effects, handlers, CSS, or backend cases (`getRecentSearches`, `clearRecentSearches`, `_addRecentSearch`) exist. Don't re-add. |
| @-prefix dropdown | Shows when text starts with `@` but isn't yet a complete valid prefix. Auto-filters as typed (`@up` → only `@updates`). Keyboard: ArrowDown/Up navigate, Enter/Tab select, Escape dismiss. |
| Client-side filtering | Sidebar `@installed`/`@updates` filter client-side (live, no Enter); `@vulnerable` is main-panel-only. Browse mode uses 300ms debounce (min 2 chars) — Enter bypasses debounce for immediate search. `browseDebounceRef` holds the timer. Stale results discarded via backend `_latestSearchQuery` guard. |
| `searchModeRef` for handlers | `searchMode` is derived via `useMemo`, so stale in `useCallback([])`. Use `searchModeRef.current` in handlers. Same pattern as `selectedProjectRef`, `selectedSourceRef`. |
| Codicon font not in webviews | Codicon font is NOT available in webview HTML. Use `icons.tsx` SVG components (e.g., `<ChevronRightIcon size={14} />`). Never use emoji characters — they render inconsistently cross-platform. Both main panel and sidebar import from the same `icons.tsx` module. Never define inline SVGs in sidebar components. |
| `$(codicon)` syntax not in webviews | VS Code `$(name)` codicon syntax does NOT render in webview HTML — it displays as literal text. Use SVG icon components or plain English descriptions instead. |
| Icon visibility: use color, not opacity | Use `color: var(--vscode-descriptionForeground)` (muted) and `color: var(--vscode-foreground)` (hover/active) instead of `opacity`. Opacity compounds when both parent and SVG child have it (0.7 × 0.7 = 0.49 effective). |
| Section chevrons | SVG `chevron-right` icon with CSS `.section-chevron.expanded { transform: rotate(90deg) }` and `transition: 0.1s`. Not Unicode characters. |
| Search wrapper pattern | Search input is wrapped in `.sidebar-search-wrapper` (flex container with border). Input itself is transparent/borderless. Clear button is a sibling inside the wrapper. `focus-within` on wrapper provides focus ring. |
| Pending data for first open | `_pendingProjectUpdates` and `_pendingInstalledCount` are cached before sidebar resolves. `_sendInitialData()` delivers then clears them. Don't remove this caching. |
| Context menu `label.includes()` substring trap | `'Update to 8.0.5'.includes('Update to ')` is true, but so is `'Update to Version...'.includes('Update to ')`. Guard with `&& !label.includes('Update to Version')` to distinguish direct update from version picker. |
| `.csproj` file watcher must revalidate webview | The debounced `.csproj` watcher must send `revalidate` to the webview (re-fetches without clearing rows — avoids empty-state flash) AND call `checkUpdatesInBackground(true)` with force AND call `_notifyMainPanel()`. Just calling the background check is insufficient — the webview still shows stale data, and omitting the main panel notification means external changes (e.g. `git checkout .`) won't refresh the main panel. Use `forceRefresh` only for explicit user-initiated refresh (manual button), not for the watcher. The callback checks `operationQueue.isBusy` — if true, it returns early (the operation handler manages its own refresh). |
| File watcher debounce cleanup on disposal | `dispose()` calls `_cancelFileWatcherDebounce()`. Sidebar-initiated operation `finally` blocks call `_cancelFileWatcherDebounce()` to prevent stale fires after .csproj modifications by the operation itself (the handler's own `checkUpdatesInBackground` replaces the watcher's role). `notifySidebarOfChange()` (main-panel-initiated) also cancels the debounce — its `packageChanged` + scoped `checkUpdatesInBackground` already covers what the watcher would do, and letting both fire produced a visible double-reload. |
| `_forceCheckPending` preserves `skipMainPanelNotify` | When `checkUpdatesInBackground` queues a force-pending re-run, `_forceCheckSkipMainPanel` preserves the `skipMainPanelNotify` flag. If any queued call had `skipMainPanelNotify=true`, the re-run inherits it. Without this, post-operation re-runs triggered by file watcher would redundantly notify the main panel. |
| `handleUpdateAll` data source mismatch | Update count uses 3-tier fallback (`allProjectsUpdates` sum → `packageUpdates.length` → single-project lookup). But `handleUpdateAll` in single-project mode only reads `packageUpdatesRef`. Must fallback to `allProjectsUpdatesRef.current.find(...)` when `packageUpdatesRef` is empty. |
| `totalUpdateCount` 3-tier fallback | Tier 1: sum of all `allProjectsUpdates[].updates.length`. Tier 2: `packageUpdates.length`. Tier 3: `allProjectsUpdates.find(selected project)?.updates.length`. Any code consuming the update count must handle that the data may come from any tier. |
| All-projects mode is sentinel-derived | `isAllProjects` is derived from `selectedProject === ALL_PROJECTS_SENTINEL` — no toggle state to reset. Switching projects via the dropdown or QuickPick automatically exits all-projects mode. Backend guards in NuGetPanel and NuGetSidebarPanel reject sentinel in all CLI-bound handlers. |
| Sidebar ref timing on init | `state` handler must immediately set `selectedProjectRef.current = message.selectedProject` — `useEffect` ref sync is deferred after paint, so the `projects` handler's `!selectedProjectRef.current` guard sees stale `''` and overwrites the persisted project with `projects[0]`. Also clear stale data (`installedPackages`, `packageUpdates`, etc.) when the project changed. |
| `installedPackages`/`packageUpdatesMinimal` response validation | Both handlers must check `message.projectPath !== selectedProjectRef.current` and discard stale responses. The backend echoes `projectPath` in both messages. Without this, an out-of-order response for a different project overwrites the display. |
| `projectChanged` no same-project guard | The handler must NOT guard with `if (message.projectPath !== selectedProjectRef.current)`. Always clear state and re-fetch — this lets re-selecting the current project act as a manual refresh and avoids stale data when title and webview state disagree. |
| `section-content` no hardcoded max-height | Uses `flex: 1; min-height: 0;` to fill available space. Don't add `max-height` — it causes premature scroll when the sidebar has plenty of vertical room. |
| Sections independently collapsible | Both Installed and Updates sections can be open simultaneously with a `MemoizedDraggableSash` (orientation="vertical") between them. `sectionSplit` state (default 50) controls the percentage split (20-80 clamped). Sash only renders when both sections are expanded. Double-click resets to 50/50. |
| Floating version context menu | `showContextMenu` message includes `versionType`. `_showContextMenu` skips "Update to X" for floating/range. Backend already filters floating from update checks — this is defense-in-depth for the context menu. |
| `versionsCache` has no TTL | In-memory LRU cache never expires. `clearSourceErrors()` now calls `clearVersionsCache()` which clears both `versionsCache` and `workspaceCache` version entries. Without this, refresh doesn't pick up newly published versions. `checkUpdatesInBackground(force=true)` also calls `clearVersionsCache()` — without this, post-operation re-checks return stale cached versions. |
| dotnet NuGet HTTP cache stale | Refresh buttons (main panel + sidebar) now call `clearNuGetHttpCache()` before refreshing (adds 0–15s). Command Palette → `nUIget: Clear NuGet HTTP Cache` (`nuiget.clearHttpCache`) is also still available standalone. `clearSourceErrors()` already re-validates sources via `startSourceHealthMonitor()`. |

### NuGet / dotnet CLI
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| `dotnet list package` fails (NU1900) | Parse .csproj directly as primary method |
| `--source ""` error | Filter: `sources?.filter(s => s && s.trim())` |
| "Unescaped characters" in request path | Skip local sources with `isLocalSource()` |
| README not showing | Extract from nupkg via adm-zip (custom sources lack ReadmeUriTemplate) |
| Floating version metadata fails | Use `pkg.resolvedVersion` not `pkg.version` for API calls |
| Version spec guard for lock file | Only `floating` and `range` version types use lock file `resolvedVersion`. Standard versions (e.g., `10.0.2`) read directly from .csproj. Guard: `versionSpec.type === 'floating' \|\| versionSpec.type === 'range'`. |
| Unlisted update suggestions | Never use the flat-container version index alone for update candidates: it includes unlisted versions. Keep listed-only update cache keys separate from explicit version lists; retain the `versions:` prefix for cache invalidation. |
| Transitive not available | `project.assets.json` needs build/restore — use `restoreProject()` if missing |
| Transitive stale after remove | `dotnet remove` doesn't update assets.json — run `dotnet restore` after |
| Unreachable custom source blocks loading | `failedEndpointCache` caches failures for 120s (2 min). Background source health monitor (`startSourceHealthMonitor()`) validates all sources at startup and self-schedules re-checks (120s on failures, 5min when healthy). `searchPackages` uses `filterHealthySources()` to skip unreachable sources — no blocking pre-validation in the search path. `clearSourceErrors()` clears all caches and triggers immediate re-validation. Source mutations (add/remove/enable/disable) also trigger re-validation. |
| Registration API returns null/garbled | Gzip-compressed endpoint selected by mistake. Filter by `!resource['@id']?.includes('-gz-')` in `discoverServiceEndpoints`. HTTP/2 client has no gzip decompression. |
| Package details missing published/deps | Registration endpoint resolving to `registration5-gz-semver2/` (gzip). Must use `registration5-semver1/` (plain JSON). |
| .NET 10 noun-first syntax | SDK 10+ uses `dotnet package add/remove/list --project`. SDK ≤9 uses `dotnet add/remove/list <proj> package`. Per-project detection via `getSdkMajorVersion()` + `useNounFirstSyntax()`. Cache: `_sdkVersionCache` (per-directory). Invalidated by `global.json` watcher. Falls back to SDK 9 (old syntax). |
| `logBulkOperationHeader` double-formatting | When `packageCount = 0`, the method uses `operationType` as the full header string. Callers passing pre-formatted strings (all-projects bulk ops) must pass `packageCount = 0` and include trailing `...` in `operationType`. Don't pass a formatted message AND a non-zero count — it appends `${count} packages...` again. |
| `dotnet package search` always noun-first | Introduced in .NET 8.0.2xx SDK as a new command — always noun-first, no old equivalent. No SDK detection needed. |
| CLI search table wraps long values | Always use `--format json --verbosity normal`, never parse table rows. Normal JSON uses `latestVersion`; exact-match JSON uses `version`. Keep the `:json` search-cache marker so old truncated entries are not reused. |
| `execWithTimeout` maxBuffer | Set to 10 MB. Default Node.js `exec` buffer is 1 MB — large `dotnet list package` output exceeds it. Don't reduce below 10 MB. |
| Vulnerability data 1h TTL | `vulnerabilityData` Map + `vulnerabilityDataTimestamp`. `clearSourceErrors()` clears it. `fetchVulnerabilityData()` skips re-fetch within TTL. Don't cache offline metadata — prefer fresh data when sources recover. |
| Offline metadata not cached | `getOfflineMetadata()` results (with `offline: true`) are NOT stored in `metadataCache`. This ensures fresh API data replaces offline data once sources recover. |
| `_globalPackagesFolder` cached once | Resolved via `dotnet nuget locals global-packages --list`, falls back to `~/.nuget/packages`. Cached for extension lifetime — acceptable since the path rarely changes. |
| Update check pre-resolves sources | `checkPackageUpdates` and `checkPackageUpdatesMinimal` call `resolveSourcesForBatch()` ONCE before the `batchedPromiseAll` loop. This pre-resolves sources, endpoints, and auth headers — don't call `getSources()` or `discoverServiceEndpoints()` per-package inside update checking. New version-lookup methods: `getPackageVersionsFromResolvedSource()` and `getPackageVersionsWithResolvedSources()` accept pre-resolved data. |
| Multi-project batch checks pre-resolve sources once | `queryAllProjectsUpdates` and `checkUpdatesInBackground` call `resolveSourcesForBatch()` ONCE before the per-project loop and pass `preResolvedSources` to each `checkPackageUpdatesMinimal` call. Don't add per-project source resolution in multi-project loops — it causes N×(filterHealthySources log) spam. |
| `refreshScoped` in all-projects mode is optimistic | `refreshScoped` handler in App.tsx does NOT send `checkAllProjectsUpdates` in all-projects mode. Instead, it optimistically removes updated packageIds from `allProjectsUpdates` state using `message.operation` data. Only `checkAllProjectsInstalled` (cheap .csproj read) is re-fetched. The sidebar's `checkUpdatesInBackground` serves as the authoritative source for update data. Don't re-add `checkAllProjectsUpdates` to `refreshScoped`. |

### Code Patterns
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| "Maximum call stack size exceeded" | `_postMessage()` must call `this._panel.webview.postMessage()`, not itself |
| "Webview is disposed" error | Check `_disposed` flag before posting in async callbacks |
| Array mutation bugs | `[...array].sort()` / `[...array].reverse()` not `array.sort()` / `array.reverse()` |
| Property name typos break VSIX | Run `npm run package:vsix` — catches errors `watch` misses |
| Module extraction locations | Validators (`isValidPackageId`, etc.) are in `NuGetUtils.ts`. Types (`NuGetSource`, `Project`, etc.) are in `NuGetTypes.ts`. `NuGetConfigParser` re-exports `NuGetSource` from `NuGetTypes`. Markdown rendering is in `markdownSetup.ts`. Search query parsing (`parseSearchQuery`, `SearchMode`, `FILTER_PREFIXES`) is in `utils/parseSearchQuery.ts` — shared between App.tsx and SidebarApp.tsx. Shared operation functions (`executeSingleOperation`, `executeBulkInstall`, etc.) are in `NuGetOperations.ts` with `OperationContext` interface. `topologicalSortByDependency` is in `NuGetUtils.ts`. Logging utilities (`setupOutputChannel`, `sanitizeForLogging`, `logOutput`, `logSuccess`, `logWarning`, `logError`, `logBulkOperationHeader`) are in `NuGetLogger.ts`. CLI operations (`installPackage`, `updatePackage`, `removePackage`, `restoreProject`, `clearNuGetHttpCache`, SDK detection) are in `NuGetCliService.ts`. Source CRUD (`getSources`, `addSource`, `removeSource`, `enableSource`, `disableSource`), config file management, and source name generation are in `NuGetSourceService.ts`. Project discovery, .csproj parsing, installed packages, transitive dependency resolution, and `project.assets.json` caching are in `NuGetProjectService.ts`. Package search, metadata, versions, vulnerabilities, icon URLs, autocomplete, update checking, README extraction, and size fetching are in `NuGetPackageService.ts` (~1250 lines) with `PackageServiceDeps` interface for dependency injection. `NuGetService` is a facade (~1200 lines) composing these sub-services, retaining HTTP fetch methods, service index discovery, source health monitoring, and credential management. |
| `fetchJsonHttp1` redirect safety | Has `maxRedirects = 5` default — never remove. Without it, a redirect loop causes unbounded recursion → stack overflow. All redirect sites use `resolveRedirect()` (exported from Http2Client.ts) which combines status check + URL resolution + SSRF validation + same-origin auth forwarding. Never follow redirects without this function. |
| `resolveRedirect` centralized SSRF guard | Combines `isRedirectStatus()` (301/302/307/308), URL resolution, `isSafeRedirectTarget()` (blocks loopback, private IPs, link-local IPv6, HTTPS→HTTP downgrades), and same-origin auth forwarding. Used by all 10 redirect sites across Http2Client.ts and NuGetService.ts. Don't add new redirect handling without calling `resolveRedirect()`. |
| ZIP entry path validation | nupkg README extraction rejects entries with `..`, leading `/`, or `\\`. Nuspec readme paths are also validated. Don't extract zip entries without path traversal checks. |
| `fetchJsonHttp1` truncated response | `resolved` flag guards `res.on('end')` after `req.destroy()` for MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE. Don't remove — `end` fires after destroy and `JSON.parse` throws on truncated data. Same pattern exists in `fetchJsonHttp1WithDetails`. |
| HTTP/2 session pool stale cleanup | Before LRU-evicting, loop `sessionOrder` and remove entries whose session is `closed` or `destroyed`. Without this, stale map entries from error/timeout handlers count toward `MAX_SESSIONS` but are unusable, preventing new connections. |
| Concurrent mutating operations | Process-wide singleton `OperationQueue` in `src/services/OperationQueue.ts`. Both `NuGetPanel` and `NuGetSidebarProvider` call `operationQueue.enqueue(label, run, abortIf)` for install/update/remove + bulk variants. FIFO across panel + sidebar (fixes cross-panel race on same .csproj). Status bar shows `$(sync~spin) nUIget: N running, M queued`. Cap of 5 waiting; over-cap rejects with warning toast. `abortIf: () => this._disposed` is checked inside the run wrapper's try/finally. File watcher uses `operationQueue.isBusy` instead of a per-instance flag. |
| Sidebar `_forceCheckPending` | When `checkUpdatesInBackground(force=true)` is called during an in-flight check, `_forceCheckPending` queues a re-run in `finally`. Don't bypass — prevents dropped `.csproj` change events. |
| Package selection | Use `usePackageSelection` hook. Installed: `metadataVersion: pkg.resolvedVersion`. Updates: synthetic `InstalledPackage`. |
| Bulk operation notification spam | `updatePackage()` and `removePackage()` have `skipNotification` option. All bulk callers (`bulkUpdatePackages`, `bulkUpdateAllProjects`, `confirmBulkRemove`) must pass `{ skipNotification: true }` — the bulk loop's summary notification handles reporting. |
| Bulk operation per-package restore | `installPackage()`, `updatePackage()` and `removePackage()` have `skipRestore` option. All bulk callers must pass `{ skipRestore: true }` and call `restoreProject()` once after the loop **gated by `!ctx.skipRestore`** (in `NuGetOperations.ts`, where `ctx` is the `OperationContext` snapshot from `_opCtx()` at message-handler enqueue time). `dotnet add package` does implicit restore — `--no-restore` suppresses it. `dotnet remove package` does not restore — explicit call needed. When the **Restore after operations** UI toggle is OFF, suppression must apply to *both* the per-package CLI restores (already handled inside `NuGetCliService` via the snapshot's `skipRestore`) *and* the deferred bulk-final restore phase (gated at the caller — never inside `restoreProject()` itself, so the explicit "Restore" webview button stays unconditional). |
| Multi-project bulk op ordering | `bulkUpdateAllProjects` and `confirmBulkRemoveAllProjects` topologically sort projects by `<ProjectReference>` dependency order using `getProjectDependencyMap()`. Updates: dependencies first. Removals: dependents first. All restores deferred to a final phase after all updates/removals complete. Don't restore per-project mid-loop — causes C# Dev Kit "unable to restore" errors. |
| InstalledTab refresh button removed | Use header-level `handleFullRefresh` + `fullRefresh` message instead. Don't re-add per-tab refresh buttons. |
| Multi-project bulk op ordering (bulkInstall) | `bulkInstall` also topologically sorts projects — dependencies first. Same pattern as `bulkUpdateAllProjects`. |
| Bulk operation early exit must send response | Every `break` early exit in bulk operations MUST send a result message (even empty) to the webview. Without it, the UI stays in permanent loading state. |
| `browseDetailsPanelContent` useMemo | Browse results details panel JSX is memoized via `useMemo` in App.tsx. InstalledTab and UpdatesTab render their own `MemoizedPackageDetailsPanel` internally. |
| `assetsJsonCache` max entries | Capped at `MAX_ASSETS_CACHE_ENTRIES = 5` with TTL sweep. Don't remove the cap — concurrent flows can grow the cache unbounded within TTL. |

### Testing
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| UI tests leak browse state | Use `openNuGetPanelWebview()` to reset search and select Installed before assertions. Replace controlled input text with `typeIntoTestId()` (Command+A on macOS, Control+A elsewhere); never hardcode Ctrl+A. |
| VS Code API not available in tests | `vitest.config.mts` aliases `vscode` to `src/test/__mocks__/vscode.ts`. Don't import `vscode` directly in test files — the alias handles it. |
| Frontend tests need jsdom setup | `src/test/setup-frontend.ts` imports `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest` matchers and shims `acquireVsCodeApi`. Added automatically for frontend project. |
| `coverage/` inflates VSIX | `.vscodeignore` excludes `coverage/**`. Don't remove this exclusion. |
| Test file ESLint rules | `no-explicit-any` and `no-non-null-assertion` are turned OFF for test files (`src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, `src/test/**/*.{ts,tsx}`) in `eslint.config.mjs`. Don't add these rules back for tests. |
| Singleton `resetInstance()` | `CredentialService.resetInstance()` and `Http2Client.resetInstance()` exist for test isolation. `instance` fields are typed `Type \| undefined` (not `Type`). |
| Benchmarks mock HTTP at NuGetService level | Service benchmarks spy on `fetchJson`/`fetchJsonWithDetails` directly (not MSW). MSW can't intercept Http2Client's HTTP/2 or custom HTTPS agent. Use `mockServiceHttp(service)` from `setup.ts`. |
| Benchmarks run in backend project only | npm bench scripts select Vitest 5's derived `backend (bench)` project. Keep the wrapper in `src/test/benchmarks/run.mjs`; removed `--compare`/`--outputJson` flags do not work in Vitest 5. |
| WorkspaceCache spam in benchmarks | `[WorkspaceCache] Cache not initialized` warnings in stderr are expected. The cache gracefully returns early — doesn't block. |
| `benchmarks/baseline.json` is committed | Regenerate with `npm run bench:save` after performance-affecting changes. CI compares PRs against this baseline. |

# Debugging Workflow
1. Add temporary `console.log()` with distinctive prefix (e.g., `[DEBUG-XYZ]`)
2. Webview logs: Ctrl+Shift+P → "Developer: Open Webview Developer Tools" → Console
3. **Remove all debug logs** after fix confirmed — search for prefix and delete
